summary: Taildrop of interactive requests after sustained batch window consumes burst credits
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightMaps is observing repeated 429s for short interactive chat requests immediately after their nightly bulk-embed batch runs finish. The pattern shows the batch consumes sustained/burst budget for ~20 minutes, then a sudden wave of short requests (qps spikes) get tail-dropped even though console shows available burst credits recovering slowly.

Impact:
- Interactive features in production degrade for end users (~15-30% of requests receive 429 within 5 minutes after large backfill jobs).
- Customer is on a Dedicated pool and reports this impacts SLAs with their clients.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightMaps-dedicated-01) in prod-us-west (us-west-2).
- Model: open-llama-13b-v2 pinned.
- Batch job: multi-worker bulk embed pipeline (500k docs) running on schedule nightly at 02:00 UTC; background workers use same API key as interactive app.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Trigger large embed backfill with 64 parallel workers using API key K-REDACTED (same key as interactive app).
2) Observe increased sustained token consumption and burst window depletion in console.
3) Immediately after batch completes, start interactive smoke test (10 concurrent short chats).
4) ~20-30% of interactive requests return 429 within first 3-7 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows burst budget refilling but interactive requests continue to get 429s and appear 'tail-dropped' (rejected rather than queued) for a short period.
- Customer captures response headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining shows small positive number, but X-RateLimit-Reason sometimes = "TAILDROP" in edge logs.

Expected behavior:
- After batch completes, burst credits should refill and interactive requests should be served preferentially (or at least not tail-dropped) given identical API key but interactive traffic should be prioritized if configured.

Additional notes from customer:
- They intentionally did not isolate background workers to a separate API key due to rollout constraints.
- They are on a reserved dedicated pool and expected predictable behavior for mixed background/interactive workloads.

Attachments/References:
- Console screenshot timestamps: 2026-03-11T02:18:22Z -> showing burst budget timeline.
- Edge logs excerpt (pseudonymized) included below in investigation notes.
comments: Support (2026-03-12): Triage received. Assigning to infra on-call to check rate-limiter accounting and taildrop heuristics in the dedicated pool. Noted customer uses same key for batch + interactive. SLA window starts 2026-03-13.

Infra (Marcus Liu, 2026-03-13): I can reproduce approximate pattern in a staging harness by firing sustained token stream then a burst of short requests — behavior aligns with an explicit taildrop threshold that prefers quota smoothing for sustained consumers. Collecting pcap and token-allocator traces.
Customer (BrightMaps Ops, 2026-03-13): We can rotate to a separate key for background jobs if that's recommended, but need guidance for immediate mitigation so interactive UX isn't impacted tonight.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 09:45Z - Correlated edge logs show ratecontroller returned rejection code 429 with metadata 'TAILDROP' for short requests at 2026-03-12T02:18:30Z.
Token allocator snapshot: sustained_window_usage=86%, burst_window_capacity=24% at peak end-of-batch; refill_rate configured at 1 token/sec per tenant for burst lane.
Dedicated pool autoscaler did not trigger; GPUs stable. No 5xx from serving-runtime. No model fallback events.
Replay in staging: when background workers used same key, we see taildrop policy engage for short requests until burst refill leaky-bucket reaches 40% threshold (internal heuristic).
diagnosis: Root cause: Mixed workload (high sustained background ingestion + short interactive bursts) using a single API key on a Dedicated pool triggers the taildrop protection in the rate-controller. The configured burst refill curve plus the taildrop threshold causes interactive traffic to be rejected briefly until smoothing completes. Customer has not isolated background traffic into its own key/priority lane.
resolution_notes: - Create a separate API key for background bulk jobs and route that key to a dedicated background rate pool. This will isolate sustained consumption from interactive lanes.
- In Console, adjust burst refill_rate for the interactive route to a higher value for the next 24 hours (if customer agrees) to accelerate recovery after batch runs.
- Configure route-level priority weighting so interactive requests have a higher priority (weight) than background ingest, or set background ingest to use a slower refill but non-preemptive pool.
- Introduce scheduled auto-scaling of dedicated burst credit for planned backfills (we can help create a policy tied to scheduled jobs).
- Validated taildrop heuristic in staging and captured ratecontroller logs (link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ratelimiter/ttl) for customer window.
- Opened an engineering issue to expose 'taildrop' threshold in Console (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ratelimiter/issues/412).
Follow-up: Support will schedule a short config call with BrightMaps Ops to create a separate background key and adjust refill settings.
resolution: Workarounds recommended and engineering issue opened for better visibility; awaiting customer confirmation on key split and refill changes.
notes: Customer asked for a step-by-step in-console runbook; scheduling a 30-minute session.
